newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Ten killed in Pakistan violence surge.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in Pakistan violence surge.

text.p: At least 10 people, including two ethnic activists and two Sunni Moslem militants, were killed in a surge of violence in Pakistan overnight and on Tuesday, police said.
Gunmen attacked the headquarters of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) in Karachi, killing two party workers, police said.
Two activists of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) Sunni group were killed on Tuesday night at Saray Saddu, near Multan city in the central province of Punjab, police there said.
Haqiqi spokesman Younus Khan said the gunmen attacked the faction's main office in the eastern Landhi district and killed Kashif Qayum, 18, and Naveed Ahmed, 21.
Haqiqi has long feuded with the mainstream MQM, which is now part of Sindh province's coalition government.
Younus said the assailants came on foot and vanished in narrow streets after firing on the White House. "The police were there, but did nothing to stop them," he said.
Elsewhere in Karachi, middle-aged Qari Abdul Ghafoor was shot dead by gunmen, but no other details were known, the police said.
The attack followed a separate shooting in Karachi on Monday night in which five young people, including a 16-year-old girl, were killed by gunmen firing from a moving car.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility and it was not clear if the attack was politically motivated.
Witnesses said tension gripped the whole area after the shooting. Armed men took to the streets firing in the air.
More than 50 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
Police said the two SSP activists killed at Saray Saddu town -- local SSP president Chaudhry Munir Ahmed and treasure as Qasim -- were shot by four men on two motorcycles.
Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab province, where the SSP and other Sunni groups are pitted against Shi'ite Moslem factions in a feud which has cost more than 70 lives this year.

On Monday, a Shi'ite activist, Syed Iqrar Hussain, was shot dead in the Punjab city of Faisalabad and two gunmen killed a Shi'ite radio producer, Shamsuddin Haider, at his home in the southern Punjab provincial town of Bahawalpur.
A Shi'ite lawyer, Ghulam Mustafa Jafri, was shot dead in the Punjab capital Lahore on Friday.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan that cost at least 170 lives last year. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 130 million but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
